subject.title: QMD per-agent SQLite caches cause extreme disk I/O on multi-agent deployments

question: Which QMD cache/storage policy should OpenClaw pursue for multi-agent deployments: automatic maintenance on per-agent indexes, shared/namespaced QMD materialization, or an explicit reduced-write/disabled-write mode?
rationale: The source confirms the current layout, but changing it crosses QMD dependency behavior, OpenClaw storage policy, possible config surface, and upgrade/operator expectations that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Measure then add default maintenance
options.body: Run a live multi-agent workload and implement automatic cleanup/checkpoint/eviction on the current per-agent layout if it brings writes and size under control without new user-facing knobs.

options.title: Move to shared materialization
options.body: Design a shared or namespaced QMD cache layout if measurement shows per-agent indexes are inherently too costly, accepting a larger migration and dependency-contract review.

options.title: Expose an opt-in reduced-write mode
options.body: Keep current defaults and add a documented reduced-write or disabled-QMD mode for large deployments, trading automatic protection for operator control.

recommendation.title: Measure then add default maintenance
recommendation.body: Run a live multi-agent workload and implement automatic cleanup/checkpoint/eviction on the current per-agent layout if it brings writes and size under control without new user-facing knobs.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to vincentkoc and their recent merged QMD work is closest to the runtime maintenance path.
